OPENSEEK - WRITTEN OFFER OF SOURCE CODE FOR THIRD-PARTY LIBRARIES
==================================================================

1. What this installer contains
-------------------------------
OpenSeek itself is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License,
version 3 or any later version (AGPL-3.0-or-later).

The installer also contains the Windows build of the Python package "av"
(PyAV 18.1.0, BSD-3-Clause) together with FFmpeg 8.1.2 libraries (avcodec,
avformat, avfilter, avutil, avdevice, swscale, swresample) and the native
libraries linked into them. Because the FFmpeg libraries are linked with the
GPL-licensed encoders x264 and x265, the FFmpeg libraries are distributed
under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later (GPL-3.0-or-later).

Libraries, versions and licences:

  FFmpeg 8.1.2                  GPL-3.0-or-later as built (code is LGPL-2.1+; built with --enable-version3)
  x264 (core 165, git b35605ace3ddf7c1a5d67a2eb553f034aef41d55)   GPL-2.0-or-later
  x265 4.2+1-e444744            GPL-2.0-or-later
  LAME 3.100                    LGPL-2.0-or-later
  libiconv 1.19                 LGPL-2.1-or-later
  GCC runtime (libgcc_s_seh, libstdc++) 16.1.0   GPL-3.0-or-later with GCC Runtime Library Exception
  zlib 1.3.2                    zlib licence
  Opus 1.6.1                    BSD-3-Clause
  dav1d 1.5.3                   BSD-2-Clause
  SVT-AV1 4.1.0                 BSD-3-Clause-Clear (+ AOMedia patent licence)
  libvpx 1.16.0                 BSD-3-Clause (+ WebM patent grant)
  libwebp / libwebpmux / libsharpyuv 1.6.0   BSD-3-Clause (+ WebM patent grant)
  Intel oneVPL (libvpl) 2.16.0  MIT
  OpenCORE AMR 0.1.6            Apache-2.0
  winpthreads (mingw-w64)       MIT/BSD-style
  PyAV 18.1.0                   BSD-3-Clause

The licence texts are installed in the "licenses" folder inside the
application folder.

2. Where to get the complete corresponding source
-------------------------------------------------
The complete corresponding source code for all the libraries listed above,
exactly as they were built (original upstream source archives, the patches and
build scripts of the pyav-ffmpeg 8.1.2-1 build, and a manifest with SHA-256
checksums, "SOURCES-MANIFEST.md"), is published as additional assets on the
same GitHub release page as this installer:

    https://github.com/obadevyh/openseek/releases/tag/<RELEASE-TAG>

The same archives are also available from their upstream projects; the exact
URLs are listed in SOURCES-MANIFEST.md (for example
https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-8.1.2.tar.xz,
https://code.videolan.org/videolan/x264,
https://bitbucket.org/multicoreware/x265_git, https://lame.sourceforge.io/,
https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/libiconv/, https://github.com/PyAV-Org/pyav-ffmpeg).

This source will remain available at that release page for at least three
years from the release date (<RELEASE-DATE>), and for as long as we offer the
installer for download. If you cannot download it, open an issue (see 5) and
we will supply it on request; this offer is valid for any third party who
received the installer.

3. OpenSeek source code
-----------------------
The complete source of OpenSeek (AGPL-3.0-or-later) for this version is at:

    https://github.com/obadevyh/openseek/tree/<RELEASE-TAG>

4. Replacing the libraries
--------------------------
The libraries are separate DLL files (in the "av.libs" folder of the
application), not statically linked into OpenSeek. You may rebuild any of them
from the source above (for example a modified LAME or libiconv) and replace
the DLL, as long as the replacement is binary compatible. Note that the
installer's DLL file names carry a hash suffix; keep the same file name when
replacing a file.

5. Requests and questions
-------------------------
Issue tracker: https://github.com/obadevyh/openseek/issues

(This offer applies to the library source code only; it does not limit any
rights you have under the licences listed above.)
